question: Should OpenClaw core add first-class per-agent backup/restore/clone now, and what credential, transcript, and overwrite policy should that restore contract enforce?
rationale: The request is useful but rewrites sensitive persisted state and overlaps broader backup/restore work, so automation should not choose the permanent archive format or security policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor core per-agent restore design
options.body: Keep this issue open and define a core `--agent`/`--as` contract with explicit credential/session portability, rollback, and compatibility tests before implementation.

options.title: Fold into broader backup restore work
options.body: Make the broader backup/restore effort own per-agent restore semantics so the archive format, encryption, and restore modes land as one coordinated design.

options.title: Defer to manual or external tooling
options.body: Leave the core CLI whole-install scoped for now and document the risks of manual agent directory/config copying until maintainers want the larger state-rewrite surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor core per-agent restore design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and define a core `--agent`/`--as` contract with explicit credential/session portability, rollback, and compatibility tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent backup docs/test ownership and prior review context make this the best available routing owner for the product/security decision.
